open_decision: The order of the added rows (and how many times each one appears) is not fixed: the laws only need each absent starter to be present among the added rows, with no law on their order, or on repeated rows.
input: enable = false, locked = (fun _ => false), registry = [], starter list = [{id 1, adapter 1, model 1, enabled true}, {id 2, adapter 2, model 2, enabled true}]
result_a: [{id 1, adapter 1, model 1, enabled false}, {id 2, adapter 2, model 2, enabled false}] (the reference order)
result_b: [{id 2, adapter 2, model 2, enabled false}, {id 1, adapter 1, model 1, enabled false}] (the added rows in reverse order; all eight laws still hold)
reason: AddsAllAbsent and AddsOnlyAbsent are membership laws on the added rows, and NewAtEnd only fixes where the added rows go. No law fixes their order or their count, so a reversed design (or one that adds each row twice) passes every law and gives a different registry.
